newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-CLEMENS LEAVES RED SOX TO SIGN WITH TORONTO.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CLEMENS LEAVES RED SOX TO SIGN WITH TORONTO.

text.p: Three-time Cy Young award winner Roger Clemens ended his 13-year run with the Boston Red Sox on Friday by signing a three-year contract worth nearly $25 million to join the Toronto Blue Jays.

The $24.75 million deal makes the power-pitching Clemens, nicknamed "Rocket," baseball's highest paid pitcher at an average salary of $8.25 million, passing the $7.75 million a season Atlanta will be paying John Smoltz over four years.
With Boston, Clemens amassed a 192-111 record with a 3.06 earned run average and won the Cy Young award as the league's best pitcher in 1986, 1987 and 1991.
The right-hander was 10-13 in 1996 with a 3.63 ERA and led the American League with 257 strikeouts.
"It was a tough and long decision," said the 34-year-old Clemens, who made $5.5 million last year with the Red Sox, told a news conference.
The deal has an option year that could push the total to $31.1 million. The fourth year would become guaranteed if Clemens pitches regularly, reports said.
"Roger is not just a pitcher, he's a leader," Toronto general manager Gord Ash said. "He's a presence for this ball club and someone that we think is going to take us to the World Series this year."
Clemens added: "We had to think about it for quite some time, but I know this was the right thing. I'm working for that world championship ring, so I'm extremely happy."
The World Series champion New York Yankees and the Red Sox were in the running to sign Clemens until the end.
"It was an exceptionally close decision," said Randy Hendricks, who along with his brother, Alan, represents Clemens. "(Yankee owner) George Steinbrenner did everything right."
The signing of Clemens crowned a series of big moves by the Blue Jays, who won two World Series at the start of the 1990s before going into a slide the last three years.

Recent additions to the Toronto lineup include free agent catcher Benito Santiago, who signed a two-year $6.5-million deal, and outfielder Orlando Merced and second baseman Carlos Garcia, acquired from Pittsburgh."
Toronto also dug into the vault to keep pitcher Pat Hentgen, who won the Cy Young award last season. He was rewarded with a contract extension through 2001 that could be worth $20.5 million.
